title: Background to the Abattoir Industry: Abattoir Layout, Systems, and Processes

lessons.title: The red meat industry and the abattoir
lessons.html:
From farm to plate

South Africa has many sheep and goat farmers, from big commercial farms in the Karoo and Free State to small farmers in the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal. Their animals are sold at auctions, to feedlots, or straight to abattoirs. The abattoir turns live animals into clean, safe carcasses. The meat then goes to butcheries, supermarkets and meat processors, and finally to people's plates.

The meat chain

  1. Farmer raises the sheep or goats.
  2. Animals are transported to the abattoir.
  3. The abattoir slaughters and dresses them.
  4. The meat inspector checks that the meat is safe.
  5. Carcasses are chilled and sent to customers.

Why abattoirs are needed

The Meat Safety Act 40 of 2000 says that animals slaughtered for meat for sale must be slaughtered at a registered abattoir. This protects people from diseases and dirty meat, and makes sure animals are slaughtered humanely.

Types of abattoirs

  • High throughput abattoirs slaughter many animals each day and have big lines and many workers.
  • Low throughput abattoirs slaughter fewer animals each day and are often found in small towns and rural areas.
  • Some abattoirs slaughter only one species, for example only sheep and goats. Others slaughter cattle, sheep and pigs on separate lines.

As a small stock slaughterer, you are part of this chain. Your work affects the farmer's income, the safety of the meat and the reputation of the abattoir.

lessons.title: Abattoir layout: from lairage to dispatch
lessons.html:
The flow of an abattoir

An abattoir is built so that animals and meat move in one direction only: from dirty to clean. Meat never goes back to a dirtier area. This stops germs from spreading.

The main areas of a small stock abattoir

AreaWhat happens there
Off-loading rampSheep and goats come off the truck
Lairage (holding pens)Animals rest, drink water, and are inspected before slaughter
Stunning and bleeding areaAnimals are stunned and bled
Dirty area (skinning)Feet and skin are removed
Clean area (evisceration)Guts and organs are removed and inspected
Offal roomsRed offal and rough offal are cleaned separately
ChillersCarcasses are cooled
DispatchCarcasses are loaded into refrigerated trucks

Other areas

  • Change rooms and toilets for workers, away from the meat areas.
  • Skin store, where skins are salted or kept until collected.
  • Condemned room, where meat that is not fit to eat is kept locked until destroyed.
  • Chemical store, locked and away from meat.
  • Waste area and effluent (dirty water) system.

Walls and floors are smooth and easy to clean. Floors slope to drains. There are hand-wash basins and knife sterilizers at every work station.

lessons.title: Systems and processes in the abattoir
lessons.html:
Overhead rail system

In most small stock abattoirs carcasses hang on hooks or spreaders on an overhead rail. The rail moves carcasses from one station to the next, so that they do not touch the floor. In some plants the rail is pushed by hand; in bigger plants a chain pulls it at a set speed.

Main processes in order

  1. Receiving and lairage
  2. Ante-mortem inspection (before slaughter) by the meat inspector
  3. Stunning
  4. Hoisting and bleeding
  5. Removing the feet and head, and skinning
  6. Evisceration (removing the guts and organs)
  7. Post-mortem inspection (after slaughter) by the meat inspector
  8. Trimming, washing, weighing, classification and marking
  9. Chilling and dispatch

Support systems

  • Hygiene system: cleaning schedules, hand-wash stations, knife sterilizers.
  • Water system: only clean, potable water may touch meat.
  • Refrigeration: chillers keep carcasses cold.
  • Records: kill sheets, temperature logs, cleaning records.
  • Waste system: blood, guts, condemned material and dirty water are handled so that they do not pollute.

People in the abattoir

  • Abattoir manager and supervisors
  • Slaughter team
  • Meat inspectors and the veterinarian
  • Cleaners and maintenance staff
  • Quality controller

Key points

  • Animals for meat for sale must be slaughtered at a registered abattoir.
  • The abattoir layout moves meat from dirty to clean, never back.
  • The lairage, dirty area, clean area, chillers and dispatch each have a job.
  • Carcasses hang on an overhead rail so they never touch the floor.
  • Meat inspectors check animals before and after slaughter.
